title: Patient Care Desk Guidance: The One-Hour Express Fee on Delivery & Pickup Services Orders
content:
An express order under Delivery & Pickup Services that the free express allowance does not cover is charged an express fee, and that fee is booked on the order in the plan's charge ledger as the order's express fee.

## When an express fee is charged

- The free express allowance itself is counted as the Delivery & Pickup Services charter counts it, and an order it covers is not charged at all.
- Likewise, a patient who holds a Kestrel Care Rewards membership in active status whose level carries free prescription delivery is charged no express fee on an order that carries prescriptions, as that charter provides, and such an order is not charged at all.
- The express order concerned is the one most recently placed on the plan. An express fee is booked while its order is still the most recently placed express order on the plan; a fee left unbooked once a later express order has been placed falls outside this computation.

## Plans in past-due status

The express fee of an order placed while its plan is past due is not fixed until the subscription fee of the billing cycle in which the order was placed stands collected on the plan's ledger. Once it stands collected, the order is priced at the plan's own express fee like any order of a plan in good standing; an order of a plan that has lapsed is priced as a Kestrel Pay-Per-Delivery order and falls outside this computation.

| The order's plan | The express fee |
|---|---|
| in good standing | fixed at the plan's own express fee |
| past due, with no collected subscription fee for the billing cycle in which the order was placed | not yet fixed |
| past due when the order was placed, that cycle's subscription fee now standing collected on the plan's ledger | fixed at the plan's own express fee, as for a plan in good standing |
| lapsed | priced as a Kestrel Pay-Per-Delivery order, outside this computation |

## Booking an order fee: `charge_order_fee_01b49350`

**What it does.** Books one fee on one delivery order of a patient's delivery plan and adds it to the fees the patient has paid on that plan. One call records a single fee of the stated kind against the named order, dated today, with the stated amount; it does not decide whether the fee is owed or how much it is. Afterwards the fee appears in the plan's fee history against that order and the plan's net fees paid go up by the amount.

**How it is invoked.** The agent unlocks `charge_order_fee_01b49350` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `delivery_plan_id` | reference number of the delivery plan the order belongs to, as the delivery plan lookup shows it | id |
| `source_order_id` | reference number of the delivery order the fee is for, as the delivery order lookup shows it for the placed order | id |
| `fee_type` | the kind of fee booked | exactly one of the values below |
| `amount_usd` | the fee charged | USD, a positive number with 2 decimal places, rounded to the cent |

Values of `fee_type`:

- `subscription` — the fee of a Delivery Pass billing cycle, which belongs to a cycle and is never booked against an order;
- `same_day_fee` — the speed fee of an order delivered by same-day courier;
- `express_fee` — the speed fee of an order delivered by one-hour express courier;
- `extended_radius_fee` — the distance fee of a courier order delivered beyond the plan's free delivery radius;
- `redelivery_fee` — the fee of a redelivery that replaces a failed order.

**Return.** A receipt listing `fee_reference` (the reference number of the booked fee), `delivery_plan_id`, `source_order_id` (the order charged), `fee_type` (the kind of fee booked), `amount_usd` and `fees_net_usd` (the plan's fees paid net of refunds after this fee). A receipt carrying a fee reference means the fee was booked.

## Hypothetical illustration

An express fee of $7.84 booked on an order returns a fee reference, the order's reference, the kind `express_fee`, an amount of 7.84 and the plan's new net fees paid; the fee then shows in the plan's fee history against that order.
